QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_45

question.text: Ganga Debt AIF draws INR 100 crore at t=0. At end of Y7, it distributes INR 200 crore (single terminal distribution; no interim). Ignoring fees, Gross IRR over 7 years is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Solve 100 = 200/(1+IRR)^7: (1+IRR)^7 = 2.0; 1+IRR = 2^(1/7) = 1.1041; IRR ≈ 10.41%. The classic '2x in 7 years ≈ 10.4% IRR' shortcut — matches the 'Rule of 72' (72/10.4 ≈ 6.9 years). The Trap: 14.30% is for 2x in 5 years. 7.17% is for 2x in 10 years. 100% is absolute ROI but not annualised. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A, XXI-B all test the '2x in N years' IRR shortcut. Memorise: 2x/5y ≈ 14.9%; 2x/7y ≈ 10.4%; 2x/10y ≈ 7.2%. Manager's Pro-Tip: In IC meetings, benchmark any deal target against the 'Rule-of-72' intuition — a 7-year IC memo claiming 25% IRR implies 5x money multiple, which should trigger scepticism on exit assumptions.
